prompt: A bar magnet moves towards a coil X with its north pole leading, inducing a current in X. A second coil (with no magnet) is placed near X instead. Which situation would induce a current in X in the same direction as the moving magnet did: a nearby coil whose current is increasing so that its magnetic field through X points the same way as the approaching magnet's field, or one whose current is decreasing?
options: A nearby coil with a decreasing current, wound so that its field through X points opposite to the approaching magnet's field
A nearby coil with an increasing current, wound so that its field through X points the same way as the approaching magnet's field
A nearby coil with a steady (constant) current
Any of these would work equally well
answer: A nearby coil with a decreasing current, wound so that its field through X points opposite to the approaching magnet's field
hint: The induced current in X depends on whether the flux through X is increasing or decreasing and in which direction.
